what_it_does: Graph processing algorithms — PageRank, shortest paths, community detection — must scatter updates to and gather values from the neighbors of every graph node, and those neighbors are scattered unpredictably across memory. Standard DDR memory (the kind in every desktop computer) is designed for sequential or large-block access, not millions of tiny random reads and writes, so most of its bandwidth is wasted on overhead rather than delivering useful data. Two common solutions each have drawbacks: graph tiling (reorganizing the graph so that frequently co-accessed nodes fit in the processor's fast on-chip cache) helps reuse but does not reduce the volume of data transferred from main memory; putting arithmetic logic inside the memory chips themselves (called PIM or Processing-In-Memory) avoids some transfers but requires complex and expensive circuitry. Piccolo takes a different approach: it adds only a simple scatter-gather function inside the memory — no arithmetic — so individual values can be selectively fetched or deposited in any order without wasting the wide memory bus on irrelevant bytes. The processor-side cache and its miss-handling logic are redesigned to work with this in-memory function, allowing graph tiling and in-memory scatter-gather to be used together for the first time.
